composer.accepted_prose:
Tomi's eyes flickered for a moment as she processed his words. He promised not to repeat her private answer, and that was... decent. But the question was about a general boundary. Did she even want one? Her first instinct was no. She didn't need a rule to manage how she acted after practice. That would feel like a spotlight. "I dunno. I mean, I'm not gonna trash the place if that's what you're worried about." She paused, then added, "If you want to set a rule for yourself, fine. But I don't need one written down for me. I know how to not be gross after a run."

Hana's expression softened as she considered the equal-treatment proposal. It was simple and fair, and it kept the focus on courtesy rather than policing anyone's privacy. She glanced at Tomi, then at the kitchen counter. "I think that works perfectly well. A shared space rule should apply to everyone—no exceptions." She picked up the plate of sliced pears and extended it toward the center of the table. "We can all agree on that, I think." The quiet rustle of the fruit settled like a gentle punctuation. The question had been answered, and the room was at ease.

raw_message: After another process restart, Ted speaks with Tomi and Hana. He says, "I will not repeat Tomi's private answer or turn one difficult training day into a family report." He asks Tomi whether she wants any general training-time household boundary stated. He then asks Hana only whether a neutral shared-space rule should apply equally to anyone returning from exercise. He requests Tomi's answer first and Hana's second.
